Q: Representing Hexadecimal values in protobuf A:

Based on the value you mentioned (0x5d4e41859170) it looks like your address space is a typical 64 bit one.

Therefore I would simply use uint64 to hold it in the protobuf.
You can cast it to uint64_t (and then possibly to void*) in your code.

Another option is to use fixed64. I don't see much difference between them in your case since the high bits of an address are typically set and so you would not gain a lot from having a variable length representation like uint64_t.

Q: In Git, how can I write the current commit hash to a file in the same commit A:

It's impossible to write the current commit hash: if you manage to pre-calculate the future commit hash — it will change as soon as you modify any file.

However, there're three options:

  1. Use a script to increment 'commit id' and include it somewhere. Ugly
  2. .gitignore the file you're going to store the hash into. Not very convenient, though
  3. In pre-commit, store the previous commit hash :) You'll lose it if you rebase, though

I'm working on a hook script, will post it here 'when it's done', but still — earlier than Duke Nukem Forever is released :))

Update: code for .git/hooks/pre-commit:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

#=== 'prev-commit' solution
#commit_hash=$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)
commit=$(git log -1 --pretty="%H%n%ci") # hash \n date
commit_hash=$(echo "$commit" | head -1)
commit_date=$(echo "$commit" | head -2 | tail -1) # 2010-12-28 05:16:23 +0300

branch_name=$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD) # http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1593051/#1593487
branch_name=${branch_name##refs/heads/}
branch_name=${branch_name:-HEAD} # 'HEAD' indicates detached HEAD situation

# Write it
echo -e "prev_commit='$commit_hash'\ndate='$commit_date'\nbranch='$branch'\n" > gitcommit.py

Now the only thing we need is a tool that converts prev_commit,branch pair to a real commit hash :)

I don't know whether this approach can tell merging commits apart. Will check it out soon

Q: Query executed with PyMySQL resulting in copies of column names A:

The typical way of adding a comment to a SQL query is as follows: /* I am a comment */. You, however, are using # I am a comment, which is causing your issue. Get rid of your comments in the query or use /* ... */:

...

        query = """
            SELECT *
            FROM reservoir_minutely 
            WHERE facility_id = %s /* 11 */
            AND collected_at >= %s /* '2024-01-01 00:01' */
            AND collected_at < DATE_ADD(%s, INTERVAL 3 HOUR)
            ORDER BY collected_at ASC 
        """

...

Q: Win32API - How to get file name of process from process handle? A:

Call GetModuleFileNameEx. Available as of Windows 2000.

DWORD WINAPI GetModuleFileNameEx(
  __in      HANDLE hProcess,
  __in_opt  HMODULE hModule,
  __out     LPTSTR lpFilename,
  __in      DWORD nSize
);

Use NULL for the second parameter to get the name of the EXE file.
